title: Polynomial reduction of diagonal derived Hom
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Choose a polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and put $C=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)[n]\in D(A)$, with the $A$-action by precomposition. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$ and $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$, and give $A$ its $B$-module structure by multiplication. Let $T\in D(A)$ be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and have finite Tor amplitude over $R$: some integers $a\le b$ satisfy $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R$-module $Q$ and $i\notin[a,b]$. Then there is an isomorphism, natural in $T$, in $D(A)$
$$\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B)\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T).$$
Here $\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}$ is restriction along the coprojection $A\to B$, not along multiplication $B\to A$. No diagonal dualizing condition on $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent polynomial-diagonal reduction using Tags 068X (perfect-over-polynomial-ring), 07VI (perfect-complex duality), 0A65 (derived tensor-Hom adjunction), 0A6A (flat base change of RHom), and 0DHS (R-perfect definition); the polynomial dualizing object is dualizing.tex Tag 0BZW. The reduction itself is derived in report.md, not claimed to be verbatim in these tags.

proof.text: If $A=0$, its module category has only the zero object and both sides are zero, naturally in $T$. Otherwise distinguish the two copies $A_1,A_2$ of $A$. Put $S=A_1\otimes_RP=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $q:S\twoheadrightarrow B=A_1\otimes_RA_2$ be induced by the presentation, and put $e=\mu q:S\to A$, where $\mu$ is multiplication. Write $a_i$ for the image of $x_i$ in $A$. Then $e(x_i)=a_i$ and $e|_{A_1}=1_A$. These identities specify every restriction used below: the output A-action will always be obtained through $A_1\to S$ or $p_1:A_1\to B$.

source.place: Ring diagram for polynomial-diagonal reduction; definitions.

proof.text: The rings $P$ and $S$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], applied respectively to $R$ and $A_1$ and their polynomial algebras. The presentation makes $R\to A$ finite type. By [lem-trf-flat-polynomial-quotient-perfect], $A_2$ has a bounded finite-projective $P$-resolution $L$. Tensoring it over $R$ with the flat module $A_1$ preserves its exact augmented sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Thus $S\otimes_PL$ resolves $B$. Each term is finite projective over $S$: a finite-free retraction presenting a finite-projective term remains a retraction after scalar extension. Hence $B$ is perfect over $S$. The same exactness calculation, using $N\otimes_PS=N\otimes_RA_1$, proves $P\to S$ flat. Also $B$ is flat over each $A_i$, since tensoring an $A_i$-module with $B$ over $A_i$ is tensoring its underlying $R$-module with the other, flat, copy of $A$.

source.place: Tags 068X and 068Y, polynomial perfectness; algebra.tex Tag 00FN and flat tensor exactness.

proof.text:
Write $D=C_{P\to A_2}(P)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A_2,P)\in D(A_2)$ and $E=C_q(S)=R\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,S)\in D(B)$, where $C$ denotes derived coinduction with precomposition action [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]. Apply the flat-base-change comparison (iii) of [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-calculus] to the finite-type Noetherian map $P\twoheadrightarrow A_2$, the flat Noetherian extension $P\to S$, and the bounded-below input $P[0]$. Clause (i) identifies both surjective-map shriek functors with coinduction, so this gives
$$E\cong B\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}D\quad\hbox{in }D(B).$$
This uses the second coprojection for this one base change; it does not replace the first coprojection on the output. By [lem-trf-perfect-complex-derived-biduality], $E$ is perfect as an $S$-complex and the canonical $S$-linear bidual map $B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,S)$ is invertible.

source.place: dualizing.tex algebraic-shriek flat base change and trivial duality; more-algebra.tex Tag 07VI.

proof.text:
For $V\in D(S)$ let $J_E(V)\in D(B)$ have the meaning of [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom]. There is a natural $B$-linear comparison
$$\alpha_V:B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\longrightarrow J_E(V).$$
Its adjunct under that lemma is $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}(B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V)\cong E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\to V$, obtained from the coinduction counit $E\to S$ of [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]. For this rebracketing take a K-flat S-model of $V$ and a K-flat B-model of $E$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; extension of the former to B is K-flat [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], so [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] computes both sides by the balanced rebracketing: $(u\otimes b)\otimes v\mapsto u\otimes bv$ and its inverse $u\otimes v\mapsto(u\otimes1)\otimes v$. Thus it uses no flatness of $B$ over $S$. After restriction to $S$, $\alpha_V$ is the perfect evaluation map $B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\to R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,V)$: at $V=S$ it is the canonical bidual map of Step 3; in general tensor that map with $V$ and apply finite-projective Hom evaluation. On a bounded finite-projective S-model $P_E$ this evaluation is the signed map $\lambda\otimes v\mapsto(z\mapsto(-1)^{rs}\lambda(z)v)$ for dual degree r and coefficient degree s, by [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model]. Its degree maps are the normalized isomorphisms of [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-degrees]; [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-differential] makes them a chain isomorphism. Hence the actual evaluation comparison is invertible, not merely isomorphic source and target. Consequently $\alpha_V$ is invertible in $D(B)$, since restriction is conservative by [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction].

source.place: Tags 07VI and 0A66, perfect evaluation; dga.tex Tags 09LN and 09LT, mixed adjunction; dualizing.tex Tags 0A70 and 0A71.

proof.text:
Choose a K-flat representative $F$ of $T$ over $A_1$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and put $V=S\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}T$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $S\otimes_{A_1}F$ is K-flat over $S$. The tensor computations of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] therefore give
$$B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\cong B\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}T$$
as $B$-objects: on these models the map is $b\otimes(s\otimes t)\mapsto bs\otimes t$. These maps are the canonical derived comparisons, so are natural independently of the resolution. For this $V$, Step 4 identifies precisely the induced coefficient complex in the question with $J_E(V)$.

source.place: Tag 08YU, lemma-double-base-change, expanded on K-flat representatives.

proof.text:
The same K-flat computation gives $A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E\cong D$ as $S$-objects through $e$. Explicitly choose a K-flat flat-term $A_2$-representative $G$ of $D$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By Step 3, $E$ is represented by $B\otimes_{A_2}G$, which is K-flat over $B$ by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Thus [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] computes its tensor with $A$ by
$$A\otimes_B(B\otimes_{A_2}G)\xrightarrow{\sim}G,\qquad c\otimes(b\otimes g)\longmapsto c\mu(b)g.$$
For $s=a\otimes p\in S$, its action on the right is $a\bar p$, exactly $e(s)$. In particular the $S$-action is the graph action, not merely the action through $P$.

Apply [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom] with $X=A[0]\in D(B)$, the $E$ of Step 3 and the $V$ of Step 5. It makes no flatness or finite-Tor assumption on $X$ or $E$ over $B$. Steps 4--6 give, after restriction along $A_1\to S$, a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}B)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{A_1\to S}R\operatorname{Hom}_S(D,V).$$
This is the actual mixed-ring adjunction, not the same-ring internal-Hom formula with a changed ring symbol.

The kernel of $e:S\to A$ is generated by $f_i=x_i-a_i$. Successively evaluating $x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}$ identifies $S/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ with $A[x_i,\ldots,x_n]$. Multiplication by $x_i-a_i$ is injective there: a nonzero polynomial has a highest power of $x_i$ with nonzero coefficient, and the monic product has that same nonzero coefficient one degree higher. The final quotient is $A$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] shows that this sequence is Koszul-regular. The augmented Koszul complex is therefore a bounded finite-free resolution of $A$ over $S$, including the empty sequence when $n=0$.

Let $H=C_e(S)\in D(A)$. The bounded Koszul resolution from Step 8 computes its underlying $S$-linear derived Hom by [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model]. By [lem-sc-koszul-complementary-equivalences], the dual Koszul complex has cohomology only in degree $n$, where it is $S/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=A$, with the ordered top-wedge generator. Restricting to $A_1\to S$ preserves this computation. This restriction is exactly the underlying $A$-object $H$, because $e|_{A_1}=1_A$: on the coinduction model $\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,I)$, precomposing by $a$ equals postmultiplication by its lift $a\otimes1\in S$. Thus $H^n(H)\cong A$ as $A$-modules and all other cohomology vanishes. Apply [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] in $D(A)$ to obtain $H\cong A[-n]$. This identifies the object with its A-action, not just an S-linear Ext group.

source.place: Koszul dual computation, duality.tex Tag 0BQZ; projective Hom Tag 0A66 and concentration in one degree.

proof.text:
Since Step 8 also makes $A$ perfect over $S$, [lem-trf-perfect-algebra-coinduction-tensor] applied to $e$ and $V$ gives $C_e(V)\cong V\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}H$ in $D(A)$. Use Step 9 and the K-flat $F$ from Step 5: $(S\otimes_{A_1}F)\otimes_SA\cong F$, by $(s\otimes t)\otimes c\mapsto e(s)ct$. The tensor models in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] therefore give
$$C_e(V)\cong T[-n]\quad\hbox{in }D(A),$$
naturally in $T$. The A-action on this tensor is through the A-valued factor $H$; the displayed map identifies it with the original action on $T$, because $e|_{A_1}$ is the identity.

source.place: dualizing.tex Tag 0BZE, perfect algebra coinduction; graph Koszul orientation and K-flat tensor cancellation.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] for $e:S\to A$, $X=D\in D(A)$ with its given precomposition A-action, and $Y=V$. It gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(D,V)\cong\operatorname{Res}_eR\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,C_e(V))$ in $D(S)$. Restrict along $A_1\to S$; the composite with $e$ is the identity. Steps 7 and 10 now identify the required left side with
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,T[-n])\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D[n],T)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T).$$
The shift equality is the usual Hom-complex shift formula (degree $r$ maps from $D[n]$ are degree $r-n$ maps from $D$). The graph orientation was fixed once by the ordered variables; every subsequent comparison is natural in $T$, so their composite has the required naturality. The assumptions on $T$ in the question are retained; the argument in fact required no extra boundedness or Tor condition on it.
